content.question: Why must a root ConstraintLayout use a separate closing tag rather than being self-closing in XML?

options.text: Self-closing tags cause build failures in all versions of Android
Child UI elements must be nested between the opening and closing tags of the layout container
Android Studio requires it for version control compatibility
It is a legacy XML requirement with no practical impact

content.explanation: Since the root layout is a container, UI elements are written as children between its opening and closing tags. A self-closing tag like <ConstraintLayout /> has no interior, leaving no place to add child elements.

Children must be placed between the parent's opening and closing tags.

content.question: If a ConstraintLayout is the root layout with android:layout_width='match_parent' and android:layout_height='match_parent', what exactly does it match its dimensions to?

options.text: The dimensions of the largest child element inside it
The physical dimensions of the phone's screen
The dimensions defined in the app's Activity class
The dimensions from the app theme resource file

content.explanation: As the root layout, the parent of the ConstraintLayout is the phone screen itself. So match_parent causes the layout to expand to match the exact dimensions of the physical device screen.
hints: The parent of the root layout is the device screen.
match_parent means 'same size as my parent'.
For the root (outermost) element, the parent is the screen itself.
